title: Deemed Continued Eligibility in the Special Needs Plans Category
content:
A member who loses the status their Special Needs Plan rests on does not lose their cover at once: a deemed continued eligibility period begins, during which every benefit is paid exactly as before.

## 1. When the deemed period has run out

> The deemed continued eligibility period has run out, counted in whole months from the date the plan last confirmed the qualifying special need.

The clock starts from the date the plan last confirmed the qualifying special need, as the enrollment record holds that date, and the length is the number of months the member's package in the Special Needs Plans category fixes. Calendar months are counted from the day of the month the need was last confirmed, a month with no matching day ends on its last day, the final day of the deemed period is itself inside it, and calendar days are never used in place of calendar months. The comparison is not-earlier-than: the condition is met on a handling date not earlier than the date reached by adding the package's months to the date of last confirmation, and a handling date falling exactly on that date meets it. The condition is tested on the enrollment record, matched to the enrollment being ended, before the enrollment is ended, and on the dates that record holds.

## 2. Counting the months, on hypothetical dates

Take a need last confirmed on the 12th of a month, and a package fixing some whole number of months.

- The period is counted to the 12th of the month that many months later.
- On the day before that day, the period has not run out.
- On that day itself, the period has run out, equality at the boundary satisfying the comparison.

Take instead a need last confirmed on the 31st of a month, where the month reached by the count has only 30 days. That month having no matching day, the period is counted to the 30th, the last day of that month.

## 3. What is done when the period begins

The plan writes to the member on the day the deemed period begins, saying what has happened, what they must do, and the exact date cover would end.

## 4. The status confirmed again inside the period

Where the qualifying status is confirmed again at any point inside the period the enrollment returns to ordinary standing with no gap, no new assessment and no fresh election.

## 5. The period ending unconfirmed

A member whose deemed period ends unconfirmed is disenrolled, given the special election period their circumstances allow, and told plainly what cover they will have in the meantime.

## 6. Cost share while the period runs

Cost-share protection carries on through the deemed period on the packages that give it, so a member is never billed cost share while their Medicaid status is being sorted out.
